description:
kith-peer/src/lib.rs:656: production code uses unreachable!() in a match arm for the "kind" field of a Peer/receipt request.

The root cause: "kind" is parsed as a String (validated at line 543 against the literals "delivered" and "read"), then re-matched as a str at line 632. The wildcard arm at line 656 is logically unreachable but cannot be proven by the compiler.

Fix: introduce an enum ReceiptKind { Delivered, Read } and parse the string to this enum once at the validation site (returning an error for unknown kinds). Then match on ReceiptKind, eliminating the _ => unreachable! arm entirely. The compiler can then prove exhaustiveness.

This is idiomatic Rust: parse-dont-validate, then match on a type-safe enum.
title: unreachable! in kith-peer ReceiptHandler can be eliminated with enum
